correctness.rationale: For each n>=1 faces are arc sets with in/out degree at most one and no antiparallel pair; underlying undirected tree excludes longer directed cycles. The subcomplex of outer arcs C_i,D_i is exactly (S^0)^{*n}. The first selected center arc A_i or B_i has respectively C_i or D_i as a valid toggle and gives a unique relative matching of all faces outside B_n. In the oriented Hasse graph no center arc can ever be inserted, so a directed cycle fixes its center-arc set; with the pivot fixed, every other outer arc only deletes and the pivot only inserts, ruling out cycles. Since B_n is a subcomplex, the relative acyclic-matching collapse lemma gives actual elementary simplicial collapse X(D_n) searrow B_n for all n. The join orientation z=*(C_i-D_i) yields a single integral homology line in degree n-1, S_n sign under factor permutations and (-1)^n under simultaneous arc reversal. The 0/1/2-center-arc partition exhaustively gives the claimed enumerator. Independent face construction (separate from repository verify.py) enumerated every compatible face and oriented Hasse cover for n=1..7, reproduced face counts 7,41,207,945,4023,16281,63423, B counts 3^n, pair counts 2,16,90,432,1890,7776,30618 and n=7 381024 covers; all graphs acyclic. A separate free-pair deletion simulated actual simplicial collapses for n=1,2,3. Finite computations are corroborative, not the all-n proof.
residual_risks: Numerical enumeration stops at n=7; the all-n conclusion depends on the written center/pivot monotonicity proof.
The displayed simplicial collapse need not be equivariant, and only the induced inclusion homology isomorphism is used for the character.

originality.rationale: Qualified best-of-knowledge originality for the genuinely branching n>=3 bidirected once-subdivided star, not for n=1,2 already treated as bidirected paths. Actual primary theorem hypotheses, graph topology, arc-face definitions and homology representations were compared. Caputi–Collari–Smith gives bidirected path and polygon results plus a suspension operation, but no direct implication of this all-n fully bidirected branching-spider simple collapse and integral S_n×C_2 sign character was identified. The older multipath homotopy paper and directed-acyclic graph comparison results concern orientations not containing the same antiparallel-arc 2-cycles. The published bidirected double-star record studies two adjacent hubs and does not subsume the one-hub two-edge-arm family. The Resultary record for the same underlying extended star concerns its discrete-Morse matching complex, a different simplicial complex. No claimed global novelty proof or assertion that failed searches establish priority.
residual_risks: No search proves universal novelty; an unindexed or unpublished general bidirected-tree collapse or equivalent spider classification could predate this result.
Generic matching/folding theory may supply a short proof; its mere availability is not an identified prior all-parameter statement or symmetry character.
The n=1,2 path cases are explicitly known and carry no priority claim.
The same underlying extended star also appears in studies of a different, ordinary discrete-Morse complex; conflating the two would create an invalid priority comparison.

value.rationale: A fully bidirected once-subdivided star is a canonical single-branch-hub infinite family beyond the path cases and distinct from the two-hub double stars. Determining an actual elementary simplicial collapse for every n, rather than merely rational Betti numbers or a finite census, explains the topological cancellation of center-arc faces. The natural integral S_n-by-global-reversal character and exact full face enumerator add structural invariants relevant to study of multipath complexes of bidirected trees. The result is limited to precisely two-edge arms, but this is a motivated natural family, not an arbitrary computational slice. Proof is short and uses standard matching tools, yet the closed all-parameter classification and module action are mathematically useful as reference examples/boundaries.
residual_risks: No claim of general fully bidirected tree classification or equivariant elementary matching.
Standard discrete-Morse machinery itself is not novel; value derives from its exact application to the motivated tree family.
